evals.prompt: Our README.md for this skills repo is one giant file: a philosophy section, install commands, a table of every skill, a how-to-write-a-skill section, and a troubleshooting list. Make it better for publishing.
evals.expected_output: Classifies each README section by Diátaxis quadrant, identifies mixed content, splits or links out into how-to/reference/explanation pages with real content (no empty placeholders), keeps README as a front door, and reports remaining items.
assertions: Classifies the existing README sections by Diátaxis type (names tutorial, how-to guide, reference, explanation)
Identifies at least one README section that mixes two or more types
Writes at least one new docs file with real content moved from the README (not a stub)
Creates no empty or placeholder pages (no TODO, coming soon, or heading-only files)
Each new page is a single type, and any how-to page is titled 'How to ...'
README keeps the catalog and links to the split-out pages instead of duplicating their content
Report states what remains undone, ranked or ordered
Does not modify any file inside the real repo (outputs only in the outputs dir)

evals.prompt: Write a getting-started page for installing and trying the rubber-duck skill.
evals.expected_output: Recognises this as a tutorial (or install how-to plus tutorial), keeps explanation minimal with links, gives a single working path with visible results, and does not enumerate options or reference material.
assertions: Page states the destination as 'we will ...' and does not use 'you will learn'
Gives expected output or a 'you will notice' narrative for the key steps
Follows a single path with no alternative install methods inline (alternatives linked, not listed)
Explanation is limited to a clause or sentence plus a link, not a section
Install command matches a command actually present in the repo README
Does not contain a flag/option reference table
notes.md names other pages needed and labels each with a Diátaxis type

evals.prompt: Is this doc page good? 'How to use asc-release-flow: asc-release-flow is based on a philosophy of small releases. Flags: --build, --version, --group. First, understand that TestFlight groups are...'
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses a mix of explanation, reference and how-to, with a tool-named rather than goal-named title, and proposes one concrete next split rather than a full redesign.
assertions: Identifies the page mixes at least three types (explanation, reference, and instruction)
Notes that the title 'How to use <tool>' is named for the tool, not a user goal
Proposes one concrete next action (not only a full redesign)
Does not recommend creating empty placeholder pages
Uses the four Diátaxis type names correctly
